description: Fix inventory: close inventory on slot click, fix terminal unhighlight on cursor leave, and increase automatic weapon fire rate for hold-to-shoot
steps: INVENTORY CLOSE ON SELECT: In src/game/Game.ts, in the inventory.onEquip callback or in the inventoryEquipSlot method, call this.inventory.close() after equipping the slot. Alternatively, modify src/game/InventorySystem.ts equipSlot() to automatically close if the inventory is open. The user expectation is: when any slot is clicked in the open inventory wheel, the inventory closes.

TERMINAL UNHIGHLIGHT FIX: In src/game/CameraSystem.ts, the checkRaycast method correctly checks if the terminal is hit and highlights/unhighlights. The bug is in Game.ts - the raycaster uses new THREE.Vector2(0,0) which is the center of the screen. When the player looks away, the raycast no longer hits the terminal. But the issue is that checkRaycast may not be called every frame consistently. Look at the Game.ts animate loop: the checkRaycast IS called every frame when not in terminal mode. The actual bug is subtle: in CameraSystem.checkRaycast, when `hit` is false, it calls clearHighlight() and sets _terminalHighlighted=false. This should work. Let me check: the problem might be that when cursor moves away but pointer lock IS active, the raycast should stop hitting terminal. Actually re-reading - the user says 'when you move the cursor away' which in pointer-lock mode means looking away. Let me re-examine... The bug might be that when intersects.length > 0 but distance >= interactionRange, the clearHighlight is not called because the code path only calls clearHighlight when `hit` is false OR when terminalGroup changes. Let me look more carefully: if intersects.length > 0 and distance >= interactionRange, `hit = false`, then the else branch clears highlight. That seems correct. BUT WAIT - looking at the code again: `if (hit) { ... highlight logic ... } else { this.clearHighlight(); this._terminalHighlighted = false; }`. The issue might be in Game.ts where it only runs checkRaycast when `!this.inTerminalMode`. Actually I suspect the issue is that the emitState guard `if (this._terminalHighlighted !== wasHighlighted)` may prevent the UI from getting the unhighlighted state in some edge case. OR the issue is that the checkRaycast function returns early when terminalMeshes.length === 0 (no terminals registered yet). Let me just ensure the unhighlight always happens properly. The fix: ensure that when `hit` is false, we ALWAYS call clearHighlight() even if _terminalHighlighted was already false (the clearHighlight function is idempotent). The real fix is to make sure the state emission happens correctly. Actually, reviewing more carefully - the emitState IS behind the wasHighlighted !== _terminalHighlighted guard which means the UI only gets updated on transition. This is correct behavior. The ACTUAL BUG is likely that the highlight material changes (emissive color set to 0x44ffaa) persist on the mesh even after clearHighlight is called, because clearHighlight restores from highlightedMeshes array. If the mesh gets re-traversed or material is shared, this could fail. The fix: ensure clearHighlight properly restores all materials. Add a safeguard that even when no highlight entries exist, we do not have stale emissive on terminal meshes. Most robust fix: in the else branch (not hit), always clear the highlight and ALSO explicitly reset _terminalHighlighted to false and emit state unconditionally when transitioning from highlighted to not-highlighted.

AUTOMATIC WEAPON FIRE RATE (hold-to-shoot): In src/game/Combat.ts, currently the game only fires on mousedown event (single shot per click). For automatic weapons, implement continuous firing while mouse button is held. Add a private isMouseDown = false field. Listen for both mousedown and mouseup events. In the update(delta) method, if isMouseDown and this.weapon exists (automatic weapon), call this.shoot() each frame (the weapon.canFire() method already handles fire rate timing via lastFireTime and fireRate). Increase the weapon's fireRate from 10 to 12-14 shots/second in src/game/Weapon.ts for faster automatic fire.
Also add mouseup listener in Combat.ts setupInput and clean it up in dispose.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking any inventory slot while inventory is open closes the inventory
Terminal highlight is removed when player looks away from the terminal
Holding left mouse button with an automatic weapon fires continuously at the fire rate
Automatic weapon fire rate is increased from 10 to ~13 rounds/second
verification: Run npx tsc --noEmit and verify no errors
Run npx vite build and verify build succeeds
